jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
Organization: Cambridge Memorial Hospital
Position: Director, Finance
Location: Cambridge, ON (on-site)
Salary: $155,000 - $185,000

THE ORGANIZATION
Cambridge Memorial Hospital (CMH) is more than a hospital: they are a cornerstone of a vibrant, rapidly growing community and an organization in transformation. Following a major redevelopment and expansion, CMH is redefining what exceptional community healthcare looks like, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care while building for the future. CMH is building healthier communities together . As a thriving acute care hospital serving the Waterloo Wellington Region and beyond, CMH provides comprehensive services including Emergency, Surgery, Medicine, Women’s and Children’s Health, Intensive Care, and Mental Health.

As healthcare continues to evolve, CMH is seeking an accomplished and forward-thinking Director, Finance to join our senior leadership team. This is a rare opportunity to influence strategy at an organization that combines the complexity of a large healthcare environment with the agility, collegiality, and impact of a community hospital.

As healthcare funding models evolve and system pressures increase, CMH is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Director, Finance to play a critical leadership role in ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability and operational excellence. This is a high-impact opportunity to serve as a trusted financial advisor to the Executive Team and Board Committees while leading a dedicated finance team in delivering robust financial stewardship in a complex healthcare environment

THE OPPORTUNITY
Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Services & Chief Financial Officer the Director, Finance provides enterprise-wide leadership and oversight of the hospital’s financial operations, planning, reporting, treasury, and internal control environment.
Working at the intersection of finance, operations, and strategy, the Director will help guide the organization through evolving funding models, growth opportunities, capital investments, and system transformation initiatives.

The Director is responsible for advancing financial strategy, strengthening fiscal stewardship, optimizing funding opportunities, and ensuring regulatory compliance, while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. As a key leader, the Director partners closely with clinical and operational leaders to align financial planning with organizational priorities. This role extends far beyond traditional financial oversight.

The Director is a trusted advisor and business partner who helps shape organizational strategy, supports critical decision-making, identifies opportunities for innovation and efficiency, and ensures CMH remains well-positioned to thrive in an increasingly complex healthcare environment.

As Director, Finance, you will drive strategic decision-making through:
Providing financial leadership and insight to the Executive Team, Directors' Council, and Board Committees, ensuring leaders have the information and analysis needed to make confident, informed decisions.
Leading long-range financial planning, capital planning, and sustainability strategies that support CMH's vision for growth and excellence.
Navigating evolving provincial funding models and healthcare priorities while identifying opportunities to optimize resources and strengthen organizational performance.
Developing and mentoring an engaged, talented finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Collaborating closely with clinical and operational leaders, the CMH Foundation, and community partners to support strategic initiatives, business cases, capital investments, and service enhancements.

IDEAL CANDIDATE
A senior leader with passion for healthcare and community impact.
Strong experience in hospitals with a minimum of 7–10 years of progressive financial experience navigating complexity and driving meaningful change.
Experience working within a publicly funded environment and familiarity with Ministry of Health reporting requirements.
Proven success leading budgeting, forecasting, audit, and financial reporting functions.
Experience presenting financial information to senior leadership and/or Board Committees.
The ability to think strategically with strong business and financial acumen while maintaining operational excellence.
Strong relationship-building and influencing skills and a collaborative leadership style that inspires confidence and trust and an ability to engage across disciplines.
Clear, confident communicator capable of translating complex financial information for diverse audiences.
Ability to lead effectively in a dynamic and evolving healthcare environment and a commitment to developing people and building high-performing teams.
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills.
Advanced knowledge of MIS guidelines, systems implementations, financial systems, financial modelling and advanced spreadsheet applications.
Familiarity with procurement practices and the Broader Public Sector Procurement Directive is an asset.
Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business, Finance, or related field.
Professional accounting designation (CPA or equivalent).

The Director, Finance role is a current existing vacancy. LHH Knightsbridge does not use artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess, or select applicants for a position.

CMH Inclusion Statement

At Cambridge Memorial Hospital (CMH), community matters to us. We acknowledge and are grateful for the opportunity to meet, work and offer healthcare on what is the traditional territories for the Anishinaabe, the Haudenosaunee and the Chinnonton.

We are committed to providing and fostering a respectful, caring, and inclusive workplace; one that generates belonging. We want a work culture where people are free to express their authentic selves and are able to bring their best daily. That includes a workplace that is free from violence, harassment and discrimination of any kind.

We welcome all applicants and encourage members of equity-deserving groups including Indigenous and LGBTQ2SIA+ communities regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, lifestyle, age, educational background, national origin, religion, neurodiversity or physical ability. We promise to ask if needed, and to provide reasonable accommodation to you during the recruitment and selection process to ensure an equitable experience.

To support all of us in this journey, Cambridge Memorial Hospital is an employee partner with the Canadian Centre for Diversity & Inclusion (CCDI) and provides access to all CMH members to CCDI resources and education. We encourage you to reflect upon our inclusive commitment to you as we welcome and encourage you to explore a promising future career at CMH.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI & Machine Learning Engineering
jobs.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Overview

Instacart’s Enterprise AI team is building the next generation of intelligent solutions for retailers. We are seeking a Director of Enterprise AI Engineering and Machine Learning to lead the development of agentic AI products that help retailers solve complex business challenges and unlock new opportunities.

In this role, you will work at the intersection of engineering, machine learning, data science, product, consulting, and forward-deployed engineering. You will partner directly with retailers and internal stakeholders to define ambitious opportunities, shape technical strategy, and deliver innovative solutions in a rapidly evolving, zero-to-one product environment.

This is an opportunity to help establish a new area of innovation at Instacart while leading teams through the full product development lifecycle—from identifying customer needs and exploring emerging technologies to building, deploying, and scaling production-ready AI systems.

About The Job

Lead the engineering and machine learning strategy for agentic AI solutions designed to address the needs of Instacart’s retail partners.
Build, mentor, and inspire high-performing engineering and science teams, creating an environment that supports technical excellence, experimentation, and strong execution.
Partner directly with retailers, product leaders, consultants, data scientists, machine learning engineers, and forward-deployed engineers to translate complex business problems into impactful AI products.
Guide the development of systems that combine advanced machine learning, data, software engineering, and agentic capabilities, with an emphasis on reliability, scalability, usability, and measurable customer value.
Establish direction in a zero-to-one product space, balancing long-term technical strategy with the need to move quickly, learn from early deployments, and adapt to changing customer and business requirements.
Represent Enterprise AI across the organization, communicating tradeoffs, progress, risks, and opportunities to senior stakeholders and building alignment across technical and commercial teams.

You will be joining a fast-paced environment where the technology, customer needs, and product direction will continue to evolve. Success will require comfort with ambiguity, a willingness to engage deeply in both strategy and execution, and the judgment to make thoughtful decisions while building new capabilities from the ground up.

About You

Minimum Qualifications

Demonstrated experience building and deploying agentic AI, generative AI, or machine learning products in production environments.
Experience leading engineering, machine learning, data science, or applied science teams through product development and delivery.
Experience partnering with product, business, customer-facing, and technical stakeholders to define requirements and deliver solutions to complex problems.
Strong understanding of machine learning development practices, software engineering principles, data systems, and the operational considerations required to scale AI applications.
Demonstrated ability to set technical direction, prioritize work, manage ambiguity, and deliver results in a fast-changing environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Deep technical expertise in agentic systems, large language models, machine learning platforms, or related areas of applied artificial intelligence.
Experience delivering applied machine learning products at significant scale, including systems used by external customers or business partners.
Experience leading cross-functional initiatives that span engineering, machine learning, data science, product, consulting, and customer-facing teams.
Experience working directly with retailers, commerce platforms, or other enterprise customers to translate operational challenges into technology solutions.
A track record of creating clarity and momentum in zero-to-one product environments while maintaining high standards for quality, responsible development, and customer impact.

Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work. This role is remote and the base pay range for a successful candidate is dependent on their permanent work location. Please review our Flex First remote work policy here. Currently, we are only hiring in the following provinces: Ontario, Alberta, British Columbia, and Nova Scotia.

Offers may vary based on many factors, such as candidate experience and skills required for the role. Additionally, this role is eligible for a new hire equity grant as well as annual refresh grants. Please read more about our benefits offerings here.

For Canadian based candidates, the base pay ranges for a successful candidate are listed below.

CAN

$313,000—$330,500 CAD

jobs.title: Director - Enterprise Data Warehouse and Data Platforms
jobs.description:
Position Description

We are seeking a Director, Consulting Expert (DCE) – Enterprise Data Warehouse & Data Platforms to provide senior technical, solutioning, and client facing leadership

The DCE will serve as a trusted advisor to the client while helping shape, win, govern, and successfully deliver complex enterprise data initiatives.

This is not a narrow technical specialist or delivery only position. The DCE combines deep enterprise data warehouse and modern data platform expertise with consulting acumen, architecture leadership, commercial awareness, and executive presence. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable discussing business outcomes with senior client stakeholders, shaping and estimating solutions, leading architecture decisions, and engaging in detailed technical discussions with engineering teams.

Your future duties and responsibilities

Serve as a senior client facing advisor for enterprise data warehouse, data engineering, analytics, and data platform modernization initiatives within a complex telecommunications environment.
Translate business objectives and requirements into actionable data strategies, architectures, roadmaps, and solution options.
Lead end to end solution architecture, considering data, applications, integration, cloud, cybersecurity, operations, cost, scalability, and delivery trade offs.
Architect and guide enterprise data solutions on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including technologies such as BigQuery, Cloud Storage, Dataflow, Dataproc, Pub/Sub, Cloud Composer, Dataplex, Dataform, and Looker.
Provide technical leadership across enterprise data warehousing, data modelling, ETL/ELT, batch and streaming pipelines, data quality, metadata, governance, security, and analytics.
Lead or co lead technical solutioning for strategic pursuits, proposals, RFPs, and account growth opportunities.
Develop and challenge solution scope, architecture, assumptions, estimates, resource models, dependencies, risks, and delivery approaches to ensure solutions are competitive and executable.
Orchestrate SMEs across data, cloud, applications, integration, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and operations to develop cohesive end to end solutions.
Lead or participate in architecture, estimation, proposal, and delivery governance reviews, identifying technical and delivery risks before commitments are made.
Advise on AI/ML and generative AI data readiness, including data quality, accessibility, governance, privacy, security, and responsible adoption.
Maintain sufficient hands on technical depth to challenge designs, validate assumptions, troubleshoot critical issues, and defend architectural decisions.
Mentor architects and technical leads and promote reusable architectures, patterns, accelerators, and solution assets across the team.
Partner with the DCS and broader P&L leadership to strengthen the client relationship, identify growth opportunities, improve solution quality, and develop technical leadership capability within the team.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

10+ years of progressively responsible experience in leading enterprise data warehousing, data engineering, analytics, cloud architecture, solution architecture, or related IT consulting disciplines.
Demonstrated experience architecting and delivering complex enterprise data warehouse and modern cloud data platform solutions.
Strong experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and its data and analytics ecosystem, particularly Big Query and associated ingestion, processing, orchestration, governance, and analytics capabilities.
Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, data modelling, ETL/ELT, data integration, data quality, metadata, security, governance, and analytics.
Strong SQL skills and working knowledge of modern data engineering technologies and practices such as Python, Git, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, APIs, and automated testing/deployment.
Experience with enterprise data technologies such as Snowflake, Databricks, Oracle, SQL Server, Teradata, Informatica, DataStage, dbt, or comparable platforms.
Demonstrated experience leading solution architecture for significant client engagements, proposals, RFPs, or complex technology pursuits.
Experience developing or validating solution estimates, delivery models, assumptions, dependencies, and technical risks.
Strong consulting and executive communication skills, including discovery, problem framing, facilitation, solution development, and client presentations.
Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary technical teams, influence senior stakeholders, and mentor architects and technical leaders.
Working knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI concepts and their implications for enterprise data architecture and governance.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience delivering data and analytics solutions within the telecommunications industry, with an understanding of large scale, high volume telco data environments and associated business and operational use cases.
Google Cloud certification, particularly Professional Cloud Architect and/or Professional Data Engineer, or equivalent demonstrated expertise.
Experience modernizing large legacy or on premises enterprise data warehouse environments to GCP.
Experience within a large IT consulting, systems integration, managed services, or professional services organization.
Experience supporting large, complex and highly integrated enterprise technology environments.
Commercial awareness encompassing consulting economics, solution costing, delivery risk, and value based solutioning.

Leadership Profile

The successful DCE will be a visible, take charge consulting leader who:

Leads with client and business outcomes rather than technology alone.
Has the executive presence to independently lead senior client conversations.
Takes ownership of ambiguous or difficult solution problems and drives them to resolution.
Retains enough hands on technical depth to challenge and defend important architecture decisions.
Challenges unrealistic estimates, unsupported assumptions, scope gaps, and delivery risks before commitments are made.
Works across organizational and technology boundaries rather than operating as a narrow or isolated SME.
Coaches and develops architects and technical leaders, raising the capability of the broader team.

Measures of Success

Success will be reflected in stronger client relationships, higher quality solutions and estimates, improved pursuit outcomes, reduced delivery risk, successful enterprise data initiatives, and increased technical capability across the team.

The DCE will be recognized by the client, delivery teams, DCS, and broader P&L leadership as a trusted senior advisor who connects telecommunications business outcomes, enterprise data architecture, technology, commercial realities, and delivery feasibility.

CGI is providing a reasonable estimate of the pay range for this role. The determination of this range includes factors such as skill set level, geographic market, experience and training, and licenses and certifications. Compensation decisions depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $115,000–$165,000. This role is an existing vacancy.

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

At CGI, we value the strength that diversity brings and are committed to fostering a workplace where everyone belongs. We collaborate with our clients to build more inclusive communities and empower all CGI partners to thrive. As an equal-opportunity employer, being able to perform your best during the recruitment process is important to us. If you require an accommodation, please inform your recruiter.

That same commitment to fairness extends to how we use technology. To support our recruitment team, AI tools may be used to help assess applications though they never replace human judgement. All hiring decisions remain entirely in the hands of our recruitment professionals.

To learn more about accessibility at CGI, contact us via email. Please note that this email is strictly for accessibility requests and cannot be used for application status inquiries.

jobs.title: HEAD, BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE UNIT
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about great storytelling, about exploring the issues that matter, about pushing the boundaries in new audiovisual experiences? So are we. As Canada’s public producer and distributor, the National Film Board has been telling the country’s stories and pioneering breakthroughs in virtually every field of audiovisual content since 1939. But to do this, we need a team that truly reflects the richness and diversity of Canada. If you’d like to be a part of this team—and part of the NFB’s incredible legacy—we’d love to hear from you.

Summary Of Duties

Provides leadership for the NFB’s business intelligence (BI), performance measurement and organizational reporting functions. Leads the development and continuous evolution of the organization’s business intelligence capability, including governance frameworks, methodologies, performance indicators, reporting solutions and analytical tools that support evidence-based decision making. Directs the analysis of organizational data and provides senior leadership with actionable insights and strategic recommendations on organizational performance, audience engagement, market trends, resource allocation and organizational results.

Main Responsibilities

Leads the development, implementation and continuous evolution of the NFB’s business intelligence, performance measurement and organizational reporting strategies, as well as governance frameworks and practices that support organizational priorities and decision making.
Advises the Chief Strategy Officer and senior leadership on BI, performance measurement and organizational reporting, and partners with them to develop, monitor and refine key performance indicators.
Establishes and maintains standards, methodologies and reporting practices that promote consistent and effective use of data and analytics across the organization.
Collaborates with IT and business owners to strengthen data systems, reporting tools, data flows and the management of business-critical data.
Oversees data quality, definitions and governance practices to ensure the consistency, integrity and reliability of BI and organizational reporting.
Manages the development and maintenance of BI tools, analytical products and briefing materials that translate complex data into clear, timely and actionable insights for senior leadership.
Leads performance measurement and analysis across organizational, audience, platform and marketing data to identify trends, opportunities, risks and emerging issues that inform strategic and operational planning.
Provides strategic insights and recommendations to senior leadership to inform decision making and performance improvement.
Oversees corporate reporting on production, distribution, audiences, revenue, equity and other organizational results, ensuring compliance with organizational and regulatory requirements.
Provides BI support and insights for brand, market and audience research initiatives.
Establishes priorities, allocates resources and oversees the delivery of BI services and products.
Participates in the development of BI sector priorities, planning and initiatives; communicates objectives and strategies to staff and represents the sector when dealing with internal and external stakeholders.
Leads team performance and development by setting objectives, evaluating results and fostering collaboration, cohesion and professional growth.

Required Training, Knowledge And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Information Management or equivalent.
Minimum of ten (10) years’ experience in business intelligence, data analytics, performance measurement or organizational reporting, including at least three (3) years of experience managing teams and staff.
Demonstrated experience leading or developing business intelligence frameworks, performance indicators, dashboards, reporting and strategic analysis for senior decision makers.
Strong knowledge of data systems, data modelling, data quality, reporting methodologies and performance measurement.
Strong working knowledge of Google Analytics and other digital analytics tools.
Experience with BI and visualization tools such as Power BI or equivalent.
Bilingualism in the official languages (French and English), both orally and in writing.

Skills Required

Initiative, adaptability and sound judgment, with a strong orientation toward collaboration.
Excellent analytical and synthesis skills, with the ability to translate complex information into actionable insights.
Ability to explain data, systems and technical concepts in clear, accessible language.
Ability to manage competing priorities with an organized, structured and rigorous approach to work.
Ability to build effective relationships, exercise unifying leadership, and influence and advise stakeholders through evidence, clarity and credibility.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to draft and present reports, in both official languages (English and French).

Qualified candidates who are interested in this position are invited to submit their application online, via the web page
Work at the NFB
, by OCTOBER 9, 2026.

The NFB is committed to building a skilled, diverse workforce that’s reflective of Canadian society. It promotes initiatives such as employment equity and encourages candidates to voluntarily indicate in their cover letter if they are a woman, a member of a First Nations group, Inuk, Métis, a person with a disability, or a member of a visible-minority group.

The NFB is also committed to developing inclusive, barrier-free selection processes and work environments. Feel free to advise us of any accommodation needs.

Please note that only applicants selected for an interview will be contacted.
